name: Vera Gallagher
life: “I still remember a novel finished on my fiftieth birthday.” On Tuesday, near the entrance to the Wash House, Vera stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I learned to read novels at fifty. Numbers with brackets still make me sweat.
appearance: Vera has thick, tightly coiled hair, a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, and a favorite piece of clothing, a black overshirt with pearl buttons. It usually goes with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. When somebody else has the floor, Vera presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Vera admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Vera learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To read a full wage slip without hiding the hard line.
family: Nelson Gallagher is Vera’s half-sibling. Vera asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Nelson chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *The button card*, Nelson says, “I left cufflinks on the card and came back to find someone had paired them with shoelaces.”
connections: Anthony Penn. A former pupil teaches a former teacher a deduction neither understood in school.

reactions.situation: A classmate asks for help reading a real wage slip
reactions.response: Vera sits beside the classmate and covers personal figures that aren't part of the question.
